name: Alien Gambit (vs Caro-Kann)
tagline: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Nf6 5.Ng5 h6 6.Nxf7!? – a knight sacrifice on f7, made famous by the Bulgarian streamer CM Volen Dyulgerov (Witty_Alien). Objectively unsound (about −1.5), but very dangerous in blitz and rapid.
ideas: The gambit was popularised by **CM Volen Dyulgerov – 'Witty_Alien' – a Bulgarian chess streamer**. It is a weapon against the Caro-Kann, the same opening you play as Black.

**Be honest with yourself:** after 6.Nxf7 Kxf7 the engine says Black is better by about 1.5 pawns. You play it because Black must find many precise moves in a row, and in fast games most players don't.
Black's king stands on **f7** and can never castle. Your whole plan is to **open lines toward it**: Bc4+, Nf3-e5+, Qe2, castle long, then g4-g5 and the rooks on the e- and f-files.
**e5 and h4 are magic squares** for your f3 knight: from there it gives check to a king on f7 or g6 and often forks something at the same time (a bishop on g4 or f5).
The **e6 pawn is pinned** by your bishop on c4 when Black's king is on f7. Pile up on it with Qe2 and Re1.
If Black does not play 5...h6 (for example 5...Bf5 or 5...Bg4), **don't sacrifice** – the engine says those moves are fine for Black, so just play normal chess.

lines.name: Main line: 7.Bc4+ e6 8.Nf3 c5 9.Qe2
lines.intro: The main line against Black's best defence. You will be a piece down, but Black's king is stuck on f7 and you castle long and throw your pawns at it. Learn the ideas, not only the moves.

name: Martian Gambit (vs Caro-Kann)
tagline: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 5.Ng5 Bg6 6.N1f3 h6 7.Ne6!? fxe6 8.Ne5 – Witty_Alien's second Caro-Kann weapon (2024). Unsound (about −1.3 to −1.5), but full of traps on the light squares.
ideas: Like the Alien, the Martian Gambit comes from the Bulgarian streamer **Witty_Alien (CM Volen Dyulgerov)**, who introduced it in 2024. It hits the Classical Caro-Kann (4...Bf5).
You sacrifice a knight on **e6** to wreck Black's pawns: after ...fxe6 the squares **e6, f7 and g6** are weak and Black's king has no pawn shelter on the f-file.
After 8.Ne5 the knight **attacks the bishop on g6**. Black has no pawn on f7 or h7 to protect it any more, so any slow developing move (8...Nf6? or 8...Nd7?) loses the bishop and then the rook on h8.
Your attacking pieces: **Bd3** (trade Black's light-squared defender), **Ng6** (cramps the rook on h8), **Qh5+** or **Qg4** (hit e6 and g6), and later **Re1** against the e6 pawn.
**Be honest:** with 8...Bf5! or 8...Bh7! Black keeps the extra piece and the engine says Black is clearly better. Use the Martian as a surprise weapon in fast games.

name: Defending the Alien Gambit (as Black)
tagline: You play the Caro-Kann, so you WILL meet 5.Ng5 and 6.Nxf7 online. Take the knight, then follow three rules: hit the center with ...c5, block checks with ...e6 or ...Be6, and never put your bishop on g4 while Ne5+ is possible.
ideas: **Take the knight (6...Kxf7).** The engine says the sacrifice is unsound: after accepting you are about 1.5 pawns better. Refusing just leaves you a pawn down.
**Counter-attack in the center with ...c5.** Opening lines for YOUR pieces is the best defence; trading White's center pawns takes away squares from the attackers.
**Against Bc4+: block with ...e6 or ...Be6.** Never walk the king to g6 – a king on g6 is hit by knight checks from e5 and h4 (see the Alien trap lines).
**No ...Bg4 while the knight can jump to e5 with check!** A pinned knight on f3 can still move if it gives check: Ne5+ forks the king and the g4 bishop.
**Trade White's attackers**, especially the light-squared bishop (…Be6). Every trade makes your extra piece count more. Your king can later walk to g8 (…Kg8) by itself – that is your 'manual castle'.

tagline: In your Classical Caro-Kann, 5.Ng5 Bg6 6.N1f3 h6 7.Ne6!? fxe6 8.Ne5 attacks your bishop on g6. Move it at once – 8...Bf5! (best) or 8...Bh7 – and you stay a piece up. Or avoid the whole thing with 5...e6.
ideas: **After 8.Ne5 your bishop on g6 is attacked and has no pawn protecting it.** Any 'normal' developing move (…Nf6?, …Nd7?) loses the bishop and then the rook on h8. Move the bishop first!
**8...Bf5!** is the engine's top move: the bishop is protected by the e6 pawn and controls d3 and e4. After 9.g4 go to h7 and answer Bd3 with ...g5 and ...Qd5.
**Don't grab with the queen while d4 is protected.** 8...Qxd4?? just loses the queen to Qxd4. Only take d4 when White's bishop on d3 has blocked the d-file (then ...Qxd4 is strong!).
**Simplest of all: avoid the gambit.** After 5.Ng5 play **5...e6** (or 5...h6) instead of 5...Bg6. The e6 pawn takes away the Ne6 jump and you get a normal, comfortable Caro-Kann.
Your king will often stay in the center for a while. That's OK – put pawns on e6/g5, keep pieces near the king and trade White's attackers.

name: King's Gambit
tagline: 1.e4 e5 2.f4 – the most famous gambit in chess history. You offer the f-pawn to open the f-file and build a big center. Objectively slightly worse for White (about −0.5), but playable at every level.
ideas: **2.f4** attacks e5. If Black takes (2...exf4), you play **d4** and **Bxf4** and get the ideal two-pawn center plus an open f-file for your rook.
**Play 3.Nf3 first.** The knight stops the annoying **...Qh4+** check, which is only possible because the f-pawn has moved.
Against **...g5** (Black protecting the f4 pawn), hit the pawn chain with **h4** before Black can play ...Bg7 and ...h6.
If Black declines with **2...Bc5**, don't take on e5 too early: **3.fxe5?? Qh4+ 4.g3 Qxe4+** wins your rook on h1. First Nf3, then c3 and d4.

**Honest evaluation:** the engine says Black is a bit better after the gambit, but the positions are open and sharp. Your king can be weak on the e1-h4 diagonal – always check for ...Qh4+ and ...Bc5 ideas.

name: Danish Gambit
tagline: 1.e4 e5 2.d4 exd4 3.c3 dxc3 4.Bc4 cxb2 5.Bxb2 – two pawns for two monster bishops aimed at f7 and g7. Sound enough for club play; with best defence (5...d5!) Black reaches equality.
ideas: You give **two pawns** (c- and b-pawns) to open the diagonals: the **c4 bishop hits f7** and the **b2 bishop hits g7**. Black's kingside becomes a target.
Develop fast: **Nc3, Ne2 (or Nf3), O-O**, then Qg4/Qb3, Re1 and e4-e5 ideas.
**Black's best defence is 5...d5!** – giving one pawn back to block the c4 bishop. Then the game simplifies into an equal endgame. Know this so you aren't surprised.
If Black is greedy and grabs your **e4 pawn** too, the e-file and both long diagonals open and Black's king often gets mated before it can hide.
The safe way for Black to decline is **3...d5**. Then you get a normal, equal position with an isolated d-pawn.

name: Scotch Gambit (and Göring Gambit)
tagline: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Bc4 – instead of taking back on d4, you develop and aim at f7. Sound: you usually win the pawn back with an active game. 4.c3 is the related Göring Gambit.
ideas: **4.Bc4** develops with an eye on **f7**. The d4 pawn can usually be won back later with Nxd4 or c3.
Against **4...Nf6** the push **5.e5!** kicks the knight. Black must answer with **...d5** – other moves lose material.
Against **4...Bc5** play **5.c3**: if Black takes, you get a lead in development; if Black plays ...Nf6, push e5.
**Göring Gambit (4.c3):** offer a pawn so your knight recaptures on c3. You get fast development, the c4 bishop and Qb3 against f7 and b7.
Always watch the **e-file**: after Black's e-pawn has left, **Qe2+ or Re1+** often wins time or material.

name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
tagline: 1.d4 d5 2.e4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.f3 – a pawn for a lead in development and the open f-file. Dubious (about −0.5 to −0.8), but a favourite of attacking club players.
ideas: The gambit is **4.f3**: after ...exf3 Nxf3 you have all pieces ready (Nc3, Nf3, Bd3/Bc4, Bg5) and an **open f-file** for your rook after castling.
Typical attack: **O-O, Qe1-h4**, Bg5 or Bh6, and Ng5. Black's king on the kingside is the target.
Against **...Bg4** (Teichmann): **h3** and Qxf3 – your queen on f3 hits b7 and f7.
Against **...Bf5**: **Ne5** and the pawn storm **g4, h4** chase the bishop.
**Be honest:** with careful play Black keeps the extra pawn. The BDG is a practical weapon for fast games, not a refutation of 1...d5.

**Be honest:** after **5...Nc6! 6.d5 Bb4!** Black gives back a little material and is clearly better. Learn that line so you aren't shocked.
Why play it at all? It's a fun way to learn attacking with pawns and space – and many opponents in blitz react badly.
